pedagogy.summary:
• Age/Topic — Ages 6-7 (Y2). Understand that the multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30 … 90) each represent a whole number of TENS and ZERO ones: 30 means 3 tens and 0 ones. A special, high-frequency case of two-digit place value where the ones column is empty.
• Standards — UK (DfE NC Mathematics, Y2): 'recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number (tens, ones)'; 'count in steps of 2, 3, and 5 from 0, and in tens from any number, forward and backward'.
• Standards — US (CCSS-M): 1.NBT.2c 'the numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones)'.
• Operational details — Build each decade with tens rods only (no unit cubes) and place them in the tens column with an explicit 0 written in the ones column, so the empty ones place is SEEN, not omitted. Tie to skip-counting in tens (10, 20, 30 …) so the spoken sequence and the tens count line up. Contrast a decade (40 = 4 tens, 0 ones) with a nearby non-decade (43 = 4 tens, 3 ones) to fix the role of the zero.
• Checkpoint — Tier A (age 6): skip-count 10, 20, 30 … 90 and build 30 with three rods. Tier B (age 6-7): say '30 is 3 tens and 0 ones' and write 30 = 30 + 0 / 3 tens. Tier C (age 7): match any decade to its tens representation and explain why the 0 is needed (place-holder in the ones).
bestPractices: Build decades with tens rods ONLY and write a 0 in the ones column so the child sees the ones place is filled by zero, not absent — this is the seed of the place-holder idea.
Anchor to skip-counting in tens on a bead string or number track so '3 tens' and 'thirty' and the third stop line up as the same thing.
Contrast a decade with an adjacent non-decade (40 vs 43) so the 0 earns its meaning as 'no ones', not 'nothing'.
Name the decade words carefully (thirty, forty, fifty) and connect the '-ty' to 'tens', flagging the thirteen/thirty and fifteen/fifty confusions.
Use the tens|ones chart to show that reading only the tens column gives the decade name — reinforcing column-based reading of two-digit numbers.
keyRepresentations: Tens rods alone in the tens column with a visible 0 in the ones column
Bead string / number track marked in tens for skip-counting
0-100 number line with decade stops highlighted
Tens|ones place-value chart showing 'n tens, 0 ones'
Gattegno/place-value chart row of decades (10, 20 … 90) linking each to n×10
commonMisconceptions: Treating the 0 in a decade as meaningless ('nothing there') rather than as a place-holder marking zero ones.
Reading the tens digit as its face value — saying 30 is 'three' rather than 'three tens/thirty'.
Decade-word confusion — mixing thirteen with thirty, fifteen with fifty, because the '-teen' and '-ty' endings sound alike.
Believing decades are a separate kind of number unrelated to ordinary two-digit numbers, rather than the ones-is-zero case of tens-and-ones.
Miscounting the rods and losing track that each rod is worth ten, not one, when skip-counting.

learn.summary: For ages 6-7 (Y2), help children understand that the multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30 … 90) each represent a whole number of tens with zero ones — e.g. 30 is 3 tens and 0 ones. The key insight is that the 0 in a decade is an active place-holder marking the empty ones column, not 'nothing', and that decades are simply the 'whole tens, no ones' case of ordinary two-digit place value. Build quantities with tens rods, anchor to skip-counting in tens, and contrast a decade with a nearby non-decade so the 0 earns its meaning.

activities.title: Building decades with tens rods and a visible zero
feedback: If the child says the 0 'means nothing', rebuild 30 with rods and no cubes and point to the empty ones spot: that empty spot IS the zero — zero ones. Contrast 3 and 30 to show the 0 keeps the 3 in the tens place (and, if ready, 300, where two zeros hold the 3 in the hundreds place) — zeros act as place-holders in their own place.
If the child reads the 3 at face value ('three'), count the ones inside the three rods (30) and say '3 in the tens place = 3 tens = 30'.
When the child adds the loose cube and 30 becomes 31, affirm: the 0 was doing real work holding the ones place empty; once a one is there, the ones digit reads 1.
Praise explanations that state both parts: '3 tens AND 0 ones'.
activities.rationale: Making the quantity drive the numeral while the zero is held visibly in place lets children connect the spoken sequence, the tens count, and the written form, and distinguishes a decade from a non-decade. Building with tens rods and skip-counting supports recognition of decade numbers as whole tens.
sourceClaims: Y2 pupils recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number (tens, ones) and count in tens from any number forward and backward.
1.NBT.2c: the numbers 10, 20 … 90 refer to one to nine tens (and 0 ones).
Skip-counting in tens and grouping with tens rods support recognition of decade numbers as whole tens.
learnerActions: Set up a tens|ones chart (drawn or physical) with two columns.
Add tens rods one at a time into the tens column, placing no unit cubes; after each rod, say the count aloud: 'ten, twenty, thirty …' and write the numeral (10, 20, 30).
Each time, write a 0 in the ones column so the empty ones place is seen, not left blank.
Build 30 with three rods and say '30 is 3 tens and 0 ones'; build 50 with five rods and say '50 is 5 tens and 0 ones'.
Rebuild 30 with three rods, then add a single loose ones cube and read what you have: 30 becomes 31. Describe what the 0 was doing before you added the cube.
Optionally mark each decade on a 0-100 number line or bead string so the spoken word, the tens count, and the position all line up.
activities.intendedInsight: A decade is a whole number of tens with the ones column filled by zero; the 0 is a place-holder that keeps the tens digit in the tens place and marks that there are no ones. Decades are not a separate kind of number — they are the ones-is-zero case of tens-and-ones.

activities.title: Decade reference chart — tap, reveal, and lift the flap
feedback: If the child names the wrong number of rods, recount the rods with them and match the count to the tens digit.
Reinforce the connection between '-ty' endings and 'tens' (thirty = three tens).
activities.rationale: A labelled reference anchors the pattern and vocabulary of decades as counts of tens. This is a reference/anchor: it names and displays the pattern but does not itself have the child build up the sequence and watch the ones column stay empty, so pair it with the hands-on building activity.
sourceClaims: Y2 pupils recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number (tens, ones) and count in tens from any number forward and backward.
learnerActions: Work from a chart of the nine decades (10, 20 … 90).
For a chosen decade (e.g. 30), reveal its three tens rods, the words '3 tens, 0 ones', and the spoken name 'thirty'.
Use a 'where did the ones go?' prompt (e.g. a lift-the-flap or cover) to answer: there are zero ones, and the 0 marks that.
Read across several decades to notice that reading only the tens column gives the decade name.
activities.intendedInsight: Each decade numeral maps to a count of tens, a decade name (ten, or a '-ty' word from twenty to ninety), and a zero in the ones column; the tens digit tells you which decade it is.

activities.title: Consolidation: sequence, match, and justify the zero
feedback: For thirteen/thirty and fifteen/fifty mix-ups, build 13 (one ten and three ones) beside 30 (three tens, zero ones) so the structural difference is visible, and stress the ending sounds.
For a face-value or 'means nothing' answer about the 0, return to building the decade with rods and the empty ones column.
activities.rationale: Mixed practice with deliberate decade-word distractors probes the common thirteen/thirty and fifteen/fifty confusion and checks whether the 0 is understood. This consolidates and checks the pattern but does not itself have the child construct the underlying grouping, so use it after hands-on work.
sourceClaims: 1.NBT.2c: the numbers 10, 20 … 90 refer to one to nine tens (and 0 ones).
learnerActions: Put the decade numerals in order smallest to largest (10, 20 … 90).
Match each decade numeral to a picture of the correct number of tens rods.
Fill in blanks such as '30 = __ tens' and '50 = 5 tens and __ ones'.
Choose and explain the meaning of the 0 in a decade (zero ones / place-holder), not 'nothing'.
Distinguish sound-alike pairs: thirteen vs thirty, fifteen vs fifty — say which is 'teen' (ten and some) and which is 'ty' (whole tens).
activities.intendedInsight: Children can recognise and justify decades across different representations, and can avoid confusing '-teen' words with '-ty' words.

activities.title: 'Convince me the zero matters' discussion
feedback: Accept answers that connect the 0 to 'zero ones' and to keeping the 3 in the tens place; gently redirect answers that treat the 0 as decorative.
If talk alone stalls, hand over rods so the argument can be grounded in a build.
activities.rationale: A short reasoning task can surface and articulate the place-holder idea. Because this is fundamentally a build-and-see pattern, discussion is proposed as a follow-up to manipulating rods rather than as the primary route to the insight; it articulates reasoning but does not itself have the child build the grouping.
learnerActions: Discuss the question: 'Why does 30 need a zero? What would happen if we just wrote 3?'
Use rods or a chart to argue your case: show that without the 0, the 3 would sit in the ones place and mean three.
Explain to a partner or adult why 30 is not the same as 3, and what the 0 is holding.
activities.intendedInsight: Articulating the reason makes the place-holder role of the 0 explicit: it keeps the 3 in the tens place and marks zero ones.

constraints: Keep the ones column empty of cubes when building decades, but always write the 0 so the empty ones place is seen, not omitted — this is the seed of the place-holder idea.
Tie the build to skip-counting in tens so 'thirty', 'three tens', and the third stop on the number line line up as the same thing.
Always contrast a decade with an adjacent non-decade (40 vs 43; 30 vs 31) so the 0 means 'no ones', not 'nothing'.
Each rod is worth ten, not one; watch for miscounting that loses track of the ten-value during skip-counting.
When extending the place-holder idea to larger numbers (e.g. 300), state the digit's actual place (hundreds) rather than carrying 'tens place' across every example.

The reference chart and the sequence/match/justify practice consolidate or check the pattern but do not have the child build the underlying grouping on their own; precede them with hands-on rod building.
Recognition and matching tasks check the pattern but do not require the child to construct the grouping independently; include building and verbal explanation for that.
Discussion can surface and articulate the reasoning; for this build-and-see insight it is proposed as a follow-up to manipulating rods rather than as a substitute for building.
reviewNotes: This is an agent semantic rewrite of saved teaching research without fresh source verification; sources were not re-fetched. The activities are research-informed proposals, not validated interventions.

Source claims for CCSS-M 1.NBT.2c and the NCETM materials are marked unverified in the original row; only the DfE National Curriculum claim is marked verified. Do not treat the unverified claims as confirmed.

The original rated a 2D interactive bench as 'ideal', asserted 'a static picture cannot' make the quantity drive the numeral with the zero held in place, and dismissed 3D as adding nothing. These are catalog-fit modality preferences, not established pedagogical laws; the live-ticking numeral, hopping marker, and highlighted 0 are retained as optional interaction examples that make the mechanism concrete, not as a mandatory or uniquely effective medium.
1.NBT.2c is a US Grade 1 standard while the topic is pitched at UK Y2 (ages 6-7); the age mapping across jurisdictions is approximate.

The original error-pattern phrasing 'contrast 3 vs 30 vs 300 to show the 0 keeps the 3 in the tens place' was imprecise for 300 (the 3 is in the hundreds place there); corrected in feedback and constraints to describe zeros as place-holders in their actual place.
Comparative efficacy of discussion-as-follow-up versus other sequencings is untested; stated only as a qualified proposal.

probeDeeper: Build 50 with tens rods — how many single ones is that, and how many ones cubes did you use?
If I add one more ten to 30, what do I have and how is it written?
assess.correctAnswer: The 3 means 3 tens; the 0 means there are 0 ones. So 30 is 3 tens and 0 ones.

errorPatterns.pattern: Treats the 0 as meaningless rather than as zero ones holding the place: 'the 0 doesn't mean anything'
errorPatterns.nextMove: Build 30 with tens rods and no unit cubes; the empty ones spot IS the zero. Contrast 3 vs 30 vs 300 to show the 0 keeps the 3 in the tens place.
errorPatterns.distractor: The 0 means nothing — it's just there.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: Child says the 0 is 'just there' or 'means nothing'.

errorPatterns.pattern: Reads the digits at face value: 'the 3 means three'
errorPatterns.nextMove: Represent with 3 tens rods and count the ones inside (30). Say '3 in the tens place = 3 tens = 30'.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: Child says the 3 stands for three ones/things rather than three tens.

responseLevels.gap: Reads the 3 as three ones or calls the 0 meaningless; no tens-and-ones structure.
responseLevels.full: States 3 tens and 0 ones, and explains the 0 marks the empty ones place so the 3 stays in the tens position.
responseLevels.partial: Says '3 tens' but is unsure what the 0 contributes.

assess.diagnosticPrompt: Write 30. Point to the 3, then the 0. Ask: 'What is the 3 telling us, and what is the 0 telling us? How do you know?'
assess.whatMakesItDiscriminate: A child with decade place value says '3 tens, 0 ones'; a face-value thinker says the 3 means three (things) and the 0 'means nothing'. The reason tier reveals whether the 0 is understood as marking an empty ones place or dismissed as meaningless.
